checklist.1: The name is the common Lagos name. Local names are spelled the way native speakers write them.
checklist.2: Ingredients are what a Lagos home cook buys, with realistic amounts per serving.
checklist.4: Steps follow the writing standard: in order, one action each, a cue on every cooking step, heat stated.
checklist.5: Total time is honest, including soaking and boiling meat.
checklist.6: Allergens match the ingredients. Anything usually added is listed.
checklist.7: Tags fit, and the spice level is fair for a typical Lagos palate.
checklist.8: Pairings make sense to someone from that region.
checklist.9: The description is two plain sentences with no health claims.
checklist.10: Cooked from the written steps at least once, with amounts fixed afterwards.
checklist.11: Tips, mistakes and storage are filled in, and none repeats a step.
checklist.picture: A picture that shows the actual dish and passed QA.

scout.title: Price scout
scout.intro: Reads published price reports and keeps only the prices our code can check against the page (doc 04, section 6).

scout.addHint: Read the website’s terms first. Add it only if they allow automated reading. The scout also obeys its robots.txt.

scout.addInvalid: Check the name, the website and the date. The date can’t be in the future.
scout.duplicate: That website is already a source.
scout.runHint: Paste this week’s report pages from your sources, one address per line, up to {max}. Each page takes about a minute.

scout.noKey: The scout needs GEMINI_API_KEY in Vercel.

scout.tooMany: Up to {max} pages per run. Run the rest next.
scout.noSources: Add a source with checked terms first.
